video_title: Lonzo Ball Gets Honest About LaVar, Big Baller Brand & His Biggest Career Regret

quotes.speaker: Lonzo Ball
quotes.summary_phrase: Lonzo Ball's biggest regret is taking control of his career earlier
quotes.excerpt: that would be my one regret, like taking control of my career earlier.
quotes.quote: I guess that would be my one regret, like taking control of my career earlier. But really I was just following my pops, and doing what I was told.

quotes.speaker: Lonzo Ball
quotes.summary_phrase: Lonzo Ball reflects on his father's influence on his career
quotes.excerpt: I never had no regrets, the way my pops was, I'm thankful for how he was.
quotes.quote: I never had no regrets, the way my pops was, I'm thankful for how he was. Honestly, I got to where I was because of him. I got nothing but love for him.

quotes.speaker: Lonzo Ball
quotes.summary_phrase: Lonzo Ball explains the Big Baller Brand basketball system
quotes.excerpt: we're dead ass trading twos for threes. We're down for giving up a layup and shooting a three
quotes.quote: The best way to explain it is if you play 2K. We're dead ass trading twos for threes. We're down for giving up a layup and shooting a three on the other end wide open, uncontested. We're down for giving up a layup and you putting your 5-10 guard down there to go try to battle with G on the post. But it's also like, we're going for every steal and we're trapping every corner, no matter what. That's how we played.

quotes.speaker: Lonzo Ball
quotes.summary_phrase: Lonzo Ball on the difficulty of replicating the Big Baller Brand system
quotes.excerpt: it's kind of going to tap out at college. College you can do it because the rules
quotes.quote: We came to the conclusion that it can be done, but it's kind of going to tap out at college. College you can do it because the rules are kind of, you can do some shit with the rules. That helps a lot. And on top of that, you kind of have people coming into the system in college. You're choosing to come over here and you're trusting me to get you to the next level.

quotes.speaker: Lonzo Ball

quotes.speaker: Lonzo Ball
quotes.summary_phrase: Lonzo Ball on his regret regarding his early career management
quotes.excerpt: if I can go back, I would obviously do it different. I would actually get an agent
quotes.quote: If I can go back, I would obviously do it different. I would actually get an agent, be in the meetings myself, do what I want to do. But to answer your question, it was like, I didn't like the shoes, I addressed I didn't like the shoes, but then we would get into an argument and it would be like, damn, if you don't wear the shoes, then you're going against the family.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Impact of losing KCP and Christian Braun on Nuggets rotation
quotes.excerpt: You have to almost pick and choose which and I knew so they let us run it back

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: See with the Thunder, the fact that Dort is gone, the fact that you have to almost pick and choose which, and I knew, so they let us run it back one more year. The next year we ran it back, we lost to Minnesota in Game 7.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: Were we hurt? I don't know. No, the thing is we won the championship and then they let Pope go. They let KCP go.

text_blocks.speaker: Lonzo Ball
text_blocks.text: And KCP is a vital piece.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: He is a vital piece. So Christian Braun is a really, really, really good player. When we won the chip, he was coming off the bench. He was a really big part of that championship team, but he moves to the starting two spot. And the thing that made us so unique when Pope was starting was he was the defender that Christian is, just as good, maybe better at that time, very good defender, but he's a three-point threat. Not trying to drive, not trying to do anything, but catch it and shoot. So when they put Christian Braun in that spot, it was a little different dynamic because Christian is a really good cutter, transition, he's not really trying to spot up and shoot. So now you only have me on the wing that's really catching and shooting.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: How losing KCP impacted the Nuggets' offensive spacing
quotes.excerpt: That was the beginning of our downfall
quotes.quote: I don't know why they let KCP go. That was the beginning of our downfall. We still went Game 7 with Minnesota after Tim Connelly kind of built Minnesota to try to beat us with the two bigs. Because then you put KAT on Joker and you let Rudy kind of roam. So they kind of built that team to try to beat us and they got us in Game 7. Then they let us run it back another year and that's when we lost to OKC in Game 7. That's when I got hurt. I was wearing the pad on my shoulder. My shoulder was like dislocated and stuff and we lost to OKC in Game 7. I had a terrible playoffs because I had an AC joint grade two injury. It was like a three or four-month injury, but I'm trying to play through it. I'm popping it with the numbing stuff with a needle every game. I'm trying to play through it, can't lift my arm, but we lose and I played the worst. So I'm like, okay, I'm the one that's probably going to get shipped out.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.

text_blocks.text: The first three is Stephen Curry, Kyrie Irving, and Damian Lillard. And this is like prime Dame. Like the Dame is going and getting seven.

text_blocks.speaker: Lonzo Ball
text_blocks.text: I feel that and I'm a Dame fan, but I'm cutting Dame. No disrespect.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: I'm starting Curry and I'm benching Kyrie.

text_blocks.speaker: Lonzo Ball
text_blocks.text: Yeah, I probably go same. Kyrie I just hooped with him yesterday, that dude is bro, he's Kyrie is probably the nicest as far as skill, like when you say skill, I would probably think he's the nicest to ever probably play.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: I was hooping with him yesterday and this is off of his ACL. That dude was so cold, bro. I couldn't believe how he was moving out there. I'm talking about he has no weakness, bro. And he was getting to the lane, there's all footers in there and he somehow was with the left. Bro, it was nutty. It was crazy.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: I think I'm benching Chris Paul with them lobs though. He had Blake Griffin and DeAndre.

quotes.speaker: Lonzo Ball
quotes.summary_phrase: Lonzo Ball's advice to his younger self on career professionalism
quotes.excerpt: I would say learn from the professionals and that's in all aspects of life
quotes.quote: If I can go back and give myself the best advice, I would say learn from the professionals and that's in all aspects of life. I wouldn't go in, like the way I got drafted and came into the league was like, my dad was like, BBB this, you know, type shit. If I can go back, I probably would just rock it on some stealth shit. Like get the best agency, sign with the biggest, you know, shoe brand, create the narrative, you know, do everything that's a lot more professional. I feel like the way like when I got drafted, like in my family, I was the first one, you know what I'm saying? So it was like, it was in nobody that I could really look up to and really, and I was already a quiet kid in general. It wasn't like I was going to reach out and ask people questions and shit like that, which I also would have told myself to do now. Going back then, I'd be like, don't be afraid to ask questions. Like even in school, I never, you know, I just like I figured it out myself if I, you know, had to do it that way. So I never really spoke out, but I feel like now it's cool to like, you know, ask for help.
